title: Within- and Between-Family Associations With 9-Year Change in Allostatic Load

sheets.name: Table S10
rows: Within- and Between-Family Associations With 9-Year Change in Allostatic Load

Note. Random-intercept mixed models of the Wave 2 outcome on each focal predictor's pair mean (between family, βB) and deviation from the pair mean (within family, βW), adjusting for the Wave 1 outcome and age (each partitioned the same way) and sex, with a random intercept for pair. Focal predictors had bootstrap top-20 stability of at least .60 in the 9-year change predictive model. All pairs pools monozygotic (MZ), same-sex dizygotic, and opposite-sex dizygotic twins; pairs is the number of complete pairs in each predictor's model, and MZ pairs the number of MZ pairs among them (outcome-level pair counts are in Table S4). βW is in outcome units per predictor unit, with a 95% CI from 1,000 pair-level bootstrap resamples; βW std and βB std scale the coefficient by the within-pair (between-pair) SDs of predictor and outcome. p is from the mixed model; q is the Benjamini-Hochberg value within outcome, pair sample, and layer, in bold when q ≤ .05. MDE is the minimum detectable βW std at 80% power and two-sided α = .05 (2.80 standard errors). Categorical predictors enter as indicator contrasts, estimated when at least two pairs were discordant: work status, retired or not working vs. employed; occupational group, professional or managerial or blue-collar vs. service, sales, or office; work industry, goods production, trade and transport, or knowledge and government vs. services and arts.
